proved: Two distinct byte-leaf trees of the same positive power-of-two size with equal constructed roots yield a differing leaf index and two unequal byte messages with equal hash outputs. Each message belongs to a constructed path-query list for that index.
interface: Uses the existing sha384SourceRoot, sha384TreePath and framed merkle/leaf, merkle/node, merkle/root encodings. Hash is an arbitrary 48-byte-output function; collision resistance is not assumed in the theorem.
scope: Both full trees are supplied; this is not extraction from an arbitrary root.
Context and leaf sizes have explicit u64 bounds.
Each selected path has depth+2 hash inputs by sha384_merkle_path_query_count; this is a witness-support count, not the total adversarial hashing cost.
terminal_application: The current four-scalar terminal has two pair leaves and depth1. Once typed pair serialization is injectively refined, its distinct-tree/equal-root event can be charged to the displayed concrete hash collision.
remaining: Quantitative quantum hash-binding and Fiat-Shamir reductions.
Full NEAR 1 Pgas and secure sub300000-byte feasibility.
